topics.title: Two Triplets of Lines Which Intersect in a Single Point
topics.text:
Prove or disprove the following assertion:



Suppose $a,b,c,d,e,f$ are nonzero real numbers such that the lines given by the equations \[y=ax+b,\qquad y=cx+d,\qquad\text{and}\qquad y = ex+f\]intersect in a single point.  Then the three lines given by the equations \[y=bx+a,\qquad y=dx+c,\qquad\text{and}\qquad y = fx+e\]also intersect in a single point (though not necessarily the same point).



EDIT: Assume for simplicity that $a\neq c\neq e\neq a$ and $b\neq d\neq f\neq b$.

topics.title: Reaper Game -1
topics.text:
In a stunning move, AoPS of InfinityLand has announced Reaper Game -1.



InfinityLand is where things get very weird, and Reaper Game -1 is no exception.  For one thing, every reap is a double, and there are no free reaps.  You cannot reap more than $2$ minutes, so the clock restarts at $2:01.$  You cannot reap more than $23$ times in this game; they will simply not allow it, and you will get banned.  If the sum of the number of reaps and the sum of the number of time you reaped exceeds $60$ (this game is no fun), you cannot reap anymore; you get banned.



Following these weird guidelines, what is the greatest average time you can reap to win the game and not get banned (getting banned will wipe your progress)?



Thanks for the help, wonderful citizens of FiniteLand!

My WRONG SolutionThere are 900 3-digit numbers, therefore there are 810,000 possible ordered pairs of 2 3-digit numbers. Now to solve this we will look for pairs where there aren't any carryovers. There are 45 ways to add two digits without being greater than 9. Similarly, there are 36 ways to add two non-zero digits to make a sum of 9 or less. A hexagon has side lengths 2, 2, 7, 7, 11, 11 (no particular order of side lengths- by this, I mean you have to figure out the order yourself) and is inscribed in a circle. Determine the diameter of the circle.



This was from a previous HW of mine.

The solution involves Ptolemy's and the answer turns out to be 14. Anyone have a full solution?
